title: Old Museum Frogs Solve a Vanishing Mystery
summary:
For almost 50 years, scientists did not know why frogs started disappearing from a forest in Brazil in the 1970s. Now, frogs kept in a museum have helped solve the mystery.

The main suspect is a deadly disease caused by a tiny fungus. The disease spread around the world in the 1970s and 1980s, but scientists only identified the fungus in 1999 — long after the frogs began to vanish.

A team from the Smithsonian and Pennsylvania State University tested more than 370 frogs that had been preserved in museum jars. The frogs were collected in Brazil's Atlantic Forest before and after the disappearances.

None of the frogs collected before 1979 had the disease. But more than half of the frogs collected in the 1980s did. This suggests the fungus arrived just as the frog populations crashed.

Strangely, the species that disappeared most showed no signs of the disease. Scientists think those frogs may have died so fast that few sick ones were ever collected.
why_it_matters: Frogs help keep nature in balance, and solving this mystery can help protect frogs that are still alive today.
